summary: iter331d — 9-slot Meet Our Makers (1 hero + 2 featured + 6 grid) tested end-to-end. Backend: full 16/16 pytest suite in test_iter331_homepage_rotation.py passes. Added 6 new iter331d-focused cases in test_iter331d_positions.py (default 1-2-6 layout, PATCH reshape 2-3-4, negative + oversized validation, ledger.positions dict, refill preserves hero tier, per-tier impression counters) — 5/6 pass. Frontend: MeetTheMakers.jsx renders exactly 1 hero (Kiln & Clay Studio) + 2 featured (Loom & Thread, Iron & Oak) + 6 grid cards on the correct preview host (active-project-4.preview.emergentagent.com); hero shows cover image bg, 'Featured Maker' badge, location, name, primary craft, bio blurb, and View Maker CTA; 'Browse All Makers' CTA at bottom. Admin /admin/dashboard?tab=settings HomepageRotationCard shows homepage-rotation-hero-count/featured-count/grid-count (values 1/2/6) and the OLD homepage-rotation-window testid is confirmed gone. All pre-existing admin testids (cadence, founder-toggle, activity signals, exclusion, ledger, eligibility-docs) still render.

minor.issue: Negative tier counts are silently clamped to 0 instead of returning 400. Review spec explicitly says 'negative counts rejected'. Repro: `PATCH {"hero_count": -1}` returns 200 with hero_count=0 (yielding window=8) instead of HTTP 400. Same for featured_count=-1 and grid_count=-1. Root cause: /app/backend/routers/community_showcase.py line 938 uses `max(0, min(int(payload[k]), 24))` which silently floors negatives. Fix: raise HTTPException(400, ...) when int(payload[k]) < 0 BEFORE the clamp. Per-tier upper caps (hero>3→3, featured>6→6, grid>24→24) work correctly end-to-end because of the normalization at line 400-402 inside `_rotation_config()`.

action_items: OPTIONAL / MINOR: Add explicit `if int(payload[k]) < 0: raise HTTPException(400, ...)` guard at /app/backend/routers/community_showcase.py:936 so a negative hero/featured/grid count returns 400 (matches the iter331d spec). Everything else in the spec is implemented correctly.

OPTIONAL / HYGIENE: The upper-cap in the PATCH validator uses a single 24 for all three tiers but the READ-side normalization enforces the correct per-tier caps (3/6/24). Consider aligning the WRITE-side caps to per-tier limits too so the stored value never exceeds what's actually usable — pure hygiene, no functional impact.
critical_code_review_comments: Refill-preserves-tier is well-implemented — verified live: closing the hero maker's shop_closed=true mid-period yields a new occupant in the hero slot (not cascaded to grid), while the 2 featured + 6 grid slots keep their original occupants byte-identically. This matches the iter331d spec.

Ledger.positions dict is present alongside the flat featured_slugs list on every fresh selection. Featured_slugs order = hero + featured + grid, and positions.{hero,featured,grid} arrays match the returned items[] exactly.

Position-aware impression counters: hero maker's homepage_position_counts.hero increments to 1; featured makers get featured=1; grid makers get grid=1. Aggregate homepage_impression_count also +1 across all 9. Per-tier tallies are stored (not just the aggregate), which enables per-tier fairness analysis later.

PATCH validator issue (see backend.minor.issue above): negative counts silently clamp to 0 instead of rejecting. Everything else in the spec (unknown-key rejection, cadence validation, excluded_slugs normalization, per-tier upper caps) works as expected.

Frontend MeetTheMakers.jsx is clean: 3 self-contained sub-components (HeroCard/FeaturedCard/GridCard), each guarded by presence checks, self-hides at 0 items, and every card has a `-cta` testid alongside the outer article testid — good for both e2e assertions and analytics hooks.

rca of the issue: PATCH-config negative-count silent-clamp — /app/backend/routers/community_showcase.py:935-940 does `update[k] = max(0, min(int(payload[k]), 24))` which converts -1 into 0 without raising. The other `for k in (…points…)` block on line 961 has the same pattern for boost points, but for tier COUNTS the spec explicitly asks for rejection. One-line fix: `n = int(payload[k]); if n < 0: raise HTTPException(400, f'{k} must be non-negative'); update[k] = min(n, 24)`.
